title: Red, silver and one small word
label: Brand gallery
lede: Two photographs of the 1985 packaging are on Wikimedia Commons in the public domain; both are small and undated. The launch predates the web, so there is no site capture from 1985 to show. The drawings are ours.

archive.caption: The 12-ounce can with the “NEW!” flash.
archive.alt: A red can with a silver wave, the word Coke in white and a yellow NEW! flash at the top
archive.credit: Photo: Jetijonez, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:New_Coke_can.jpg), public domain. Trademarks belong to their owners; shown for commentary.

archive.caption: A small bottle with the same label.
archive.alt: A small bottle of cola with a red and silver label reading Coke and NEW!
archive.credit: Photo: My100cans, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Newcokebottle2.jpg), public domain. Trademarks belong to their owners; shown for commentary.

blocks.title: One Coke in April, two in July

before.label: Apr 1985
before.caption: The new formula replaces the old one.[^3]
before.alt: Drawing of a single red can with a NEW flash

after.label: Jul 1985
after.caption: The old formula returns as Classic and is sold beside it.[^6]
after.alt: Drawing of two red cans, one marked NEW and one marked CLASSIC

blocks.source: Both panels are original illustrations, not photographs or official artwork. Dates: The Washington Post[^3] and UPI[^6].

drawings.title: The can.
drawings.caption: Red, a silver wave and a flash. Original illustration; it does not reproduce the logo.

drawings.title: The hotline.
drawings.caption: Fifteen hundred calls a day by June 1985, and “a barrage of angry letters.”[^1][^8] Original illustration.

drawings.title: The basement.
drawings.caption: Coca-Cola’s history describes people hoarding as many as 900 bottles of the old drink.[^1] Original illustration, not a photograph of a real cellar.

drawings.title: The pair.
drawings.caption: New and Classic, sold side by side from July 1985.[^6] Original illustration with our own lettering.

disclaimer: Colors were matched by eye to the Wikimedia Commons photographs and are approximate. Coca-Cola, Coke, Coca-Cola Classic and Coke II are trademarks of The Coca-Cola Company and appear here in historical and editorial context. The drawings are original illustrations, not official assets, and do not reproduce the logo.
